recipes.name: Chettinad Chicken Pepper Fry

steps.text: Toss the chicken with turmeric, chilli powder, half the salt, half the crushed pepper, ginger, garlic and 1 tsp oil. Marinate.
Air-fry the chicken at 200°C for 12 minutes in a single layer, shaking/flipping the pieces at 6 minutes.
Meanwhile heat the remaining oil in a kadai; crackle fennel, dry red chilli and curry leaves, then sauté the onion until golden.
Add tomato, coriander powder and remaining salt; cook until the tomato breaks down and oil separates.
Add the air-fried chicken, cumin and the rest of the crushed pepper; roast on high, tossing, until the masala coats the pieces and turns dark.
Finish with lemon juice and coriander leaves. Serve hot.

tips: Crush the pepper fresh just before cooking — it is the backbone of the dish.
For keto, serve with cucumber-onion salad instead of rice.
recipes.makeAhead: Air-fry and marinate-cook the chicken up to 2 days ahead; do the final pepper roast just before serving.

recipes.name: Chettinad Chicken Curry

steps.text: Marinate the chicken with turmeric, chilli powder and 1 tsp salt.
Dry-roast dry red chilli, pepper, fennel, cumin and coriander until fragrant; add coconut and roast till light brown. Cool and grind to a fine paste with a little water.
Heat oil in the pressure cooker; add whole spices and curry leaves, then onion and cook until golden. Add ginger-garlic (crushed) and sauté for a minute.
Add tomato and cook till mushy, then add the chicken and sear on high for 3–4 minutes.
Stir in the ground masala, remaining salt and 300 ml water. Pressure cook for 2 whistles on medium, then let the pressure release naturally.
Simmer open for a few minutes to the consistency you like; finish with coriander leaves.

tips: Kalpasi (stone flower) gives the signature Chettinad aroma — skip it only if you must.
recipes.makeAhead: Tastes better the next day; refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze in portions for a month.

recipes.name: Air-Fryer Chettinad Chicken Chukka

steps.text: Mix chicken with ginger, turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder, half the pepper, half the salt and the garlic oil. Marinate.
Air-fry at 200°C for 10 minutes, flipping at 5 minutes, until the edges char lightly.
In a pan heat groundnut oil; crackle fennel, dry red chilli and curry leaves. Add tomato and cook down for 2 minutes.
Add the air-fried chicken, remaining pepper and salt; toss on high heat until dry and coated.
Turn off the heat, add spring onion greens and lemon juice, toss and serve.

tips: Naturally low-FODMAP and keto: garlic oil carries the garlic flavour without the fructans.
recipes.makeAhead: Keeps 3 days refrigerated; re-crisp in the air fryer at 180°C for 4 minutes.

recipes.name: Air-Fryer Chicken 65

steps.text: Mix chicken with curd, ginger, chilli powder, turmeric, garam masala, pepper, lemon juice, salt and 10 g garlic oil. Marinate.
Sprinkle rice flour and cornflour over the chicken and toss until every piece is dry-coated.
Lightly brush the air-fryer basket with oil, arrange pieces in one layer and air-fry at 200°C for 14 minutes, flipping and spraying with a little oil at 7 minutes.
Heat remaining garlic oil in a pan, splutter curry leaves and green chillies, add the chicken and toss for a minute.

tips: Do not crowd the basket — airflow is what makes the coating crisp.

recipes.name: Chicken Keema Egg Kothu

steps.text: Heat oil on a tawa; add curry leaves, onion, green chilli, ginger and garlic and sauté until soft.
Add tomato, turmeric, chilli powder and salt; cook until mushy.
Add the chicken mince, break it up with the spatula and cook until no pink remains and it is dry.
Push to the side, pour in the beaten eggs and whites, let them set for 30 seconds, then chop and mix everything together with two flat spatulas, kothu style.
Finish with garam masala, pepper and coriander leaves.

tips: Great with a single millet dosa or on its own for a keto breakfast.
recipes.makeAhead: Cook the keema base the night before; add eggs fresh in the morning.

recipes.name: Kerala Chicken Stew

steps.text: Heat coconut oil in a pot; add whole spices, then ginger, green chilli and curry leaves. Sauté for a minute.
Add the chicken, salt and pepper; stir until the pieces turn white.
Add carrot, beans and 250 ml water (or thin coconut milk). Cover and simmer until the chicken and vegetables are tender.
Lower the heat, stir in the thick coconut milk and warm through without boiling.
Top with spring onion greens and a few fresh curry leaves.

tips: Never boil after adding thick coconut milk or it will split.
Naturally low-FODMAP and keto-friendly.
recipes.makeAhead: Keeps 2 days refrigerated; reheat gently on low.

recipes.name: Kerala Chicken Roast

steps.text: Marinate chicken with turmeric, half the chilli powder, pepper and salt.
Heat coconut oil in a kadai; add fennel and curry leaves, then onions with a pinch of salt. Cook until deep brown.
Add ginger, garlic, green chilli; sauté, then add the powdered spices on low heat for 30 seconds.
Add tomato and cook until oil separates. Add the chicken, cover and cook in its own juices on medium-low.
Uncover and roast on medium-high, stirring, until the masala is thick, dark and clings to the chicken.

tips: Patience with the onions gives the roast its deep colour.
recipes.makeAhead: Refrigerate up to 3 days; freezes well.

recipes.name: Kerala Air-Fried Chicken Strips

steps.text: Mix chicken with ginger, garlic oil, spices, chopped curry leaves, lemon juice and salt. Marinate (overnight is best).
Dust with rice flour and toss well so the pieces are evenly coated.
Brush the basket with coconut oil, arrange strips in one layer and air-fry at 200°C for 14 minutes, flipping at 7 minutes and brushing with the remaining coconut oil.
Add the whole curry leaves to the basket for the last 2 minutes so they crisp up.

tips: Low-FODMAP as written; serve with a lemon wedge and cucumber.
recipes.makeAhead: Marinate up to 24 hours ahead in the fridge.

recipes.name: Chicken Puttu

steps.text: Boil the chicken with a pinch of turmeric and salt until cooked, then shred finely.
Heat coconut oil in a pan; add curry leaves, ginger and green chilli, then tomato. Add the shredded chicken, pepper, garam masala and cook until dry.
Sprinkle salted water over the puttu podi and rub until it feels like moist breadcrumbs.
Layer the puttu maker: a little grated coconut, puttu podi, chicken masala, repeat, ending with coconut and spring onion greens.
Steam until steam escapes from the top, then push out the puttu.

tips: No puttu maker? Layer in a steel tumbler and steam in an idli pot.
recipes.makeAhead: Make the chicken masala the night before; steam fresh in the morning.

recipes.name: Andhra Chicken Fry

steps.text: Marinate chicken with ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, chilli powder, salt and lemon juice.
Air-fry at 200°C for 15 minutes, flipping at 8 minutes, until cooked and lightly charred.
Heat oil in a kadai; fry curry leaves and green chillies, then onion until golden.
Add coriander powder, garam masala and the air-fried chicken with its juices; fry on high until dry and red.
Garnish with coriander leaves.

tips: Fiery and keto-friendly; pair with raita (lactose-free for IBS).
recipes.makeAhead: Refrigerate up to 3 days; re-crisp in the air fryer at 180°C for 5 minutes.

recipes.name: Andhra Chicken Curry

steps.text: Marinate chicken with turmeric, half the chilli powder and salt.
Heat oil in the cooker; add curry leaves, green chilli and onion and cook until golden. Add ginger-garlic paste and sauté.
Add tomato, the remaining chilli powder and coriander powder; cook until oil separates.
Add chicken, sear for 3 minutes, add 250 ml water and pressure cook for 2 whistles. Let pressure release naturally.
Stir in garam masala, simmer for 2 minutes and garnish with coriander.

tips: Add a squeeze of lemon if your tomatoes are not tangy enough.
recipes.makeAhead: Refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze in portions.

recipes.name: Andhra Chicken Liver Fry

steps.text: Rinse the liver, drain well and toss with turmeric and salt.
Heat oil in a pan; add curry leaves, green chilli and onion and sauté until soft. Add ginger-garlic paste.
Add the liver in one layer and sear on medium-high without stirring for 2 minutes, then turn.
Add chilli powder, pepper and garam masala; cook, tossing, until just cooked through (no longer pink inside).
Garnish with coriander and serve immediately.

tips: Do not overcook liver — it turns rubbery. A rich source of iron and B12.

recipes.name: Hyderabadi Dum Ka Murgh

ingredients.note: green cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, shahi jeera

steps.text: Brown the sliced onion in the oil until crisp-golden; remove half and crush it.
Marinate chicken with curd, ginger-garlic paste, cashew paste, crushed onion, spices, mint, coriander, green chilli, lemon and salt.
Heat ghee in a heavy pot, add whole spices, then the chicken with all the marinade. Cook uncovered on medium for 8 minutes.
Seal the lid with dough or foil and cook on the lowest flame (dum) until tender.
Rest 5 minutes, open and garnish with the remaining fried onion and mint.

tips: Use a tawa under the pot during dum to avoid scorching.
recipes.makeAhead: Marinate overnight; the cooked dish keeps 3 days refrigerated.

recipes.name: Hyderabadi Chicken Pathar Kebab

steps.text: Pound chicken escalopes thin. Rub with papaya paste, ginger, garlic oil, spices, mint, lemon and salt. Marinate.
Preheat the air fryer at 200°C for 3 minutes (in place of the traditional heated granite stone).
Lay escalopes flat in one layer, brush with ghee and air-fry at 200°C for 8 minutes, flipping and brushing again at 4 minutes.
Serve with lemon wedges and sliced cucumber.

tips: Do not marinate longer than 2 hours with papaya — it will turn mushy.
Low-FODMAP and keto as written.

recipes.name: Mangalorean Chicken Ghee Roast

steps.text: Marinate chicken with curd, turmeric, lemon juice and half the salt.
Dry-roast red chillies, coriander, cumin, pepper and fenugreek on low heat. Grind with garlic, tamarind and a splash of water to a smooth red paste.
Heat 1 tbsp ghee in a kadai and sear the chicken until lightly browned; remove.
Add the remaining ghee and the ground paste; roast on low, stirring, until the raw smell goes and ghee separates.
Return the chicken with jaggery and remaining salt; cook covered on low until done, then uncover and roast until the masala is thick and glossy.
Finish with curry leaves fried in a little ghee.

tips: Byadgi chillies give deep colour with moderate heat.
recipes.makeAhead: The ghee-roast masala paste keeps 1 week refrigerated.

recipes.name: Bangalore Military-Style Chicken Kabab

steps.text: Mix chicken with curd, ginger-garlic paste, chilli powder, garam masala, turmeric, lemon and salt. Marinate.
Add cornflour and rice flour and mix until the marinade clings thickly.
Brush the basket with oil and air-fry at 200°C for 14 minutes, flipping and brushing with oil at 7 minutes.
Temper curry leaves and green chillies in the remaining oil and toss with the kababs.

tips: Skip red food colour — Kashmiri chilli powder gives a good red.
recipes.makeAhead: Marinate up to 24 hours ahead.

recipes.name: Goan Chicken Cafreal

steps.text: Grind coriander, mint, green chilli, ginger, whole spices, pepper, cumin, turmeric, vinegar and salt to a smooth green paste.
Rub the paste and garlic oil into the slashed chicken. Marinate.
Brush with coconut oil and air-fry at 190°C for 16 minutes, flipping at 8 minutes, until charred at the edges.
Squeeze over lemon and serve with a green salad.

tips: Low-FODMAP and keto. Marinate overnight for the best flavour.
recipes.makeAhead: Cafreal paste freezes well in ice-cube trays for 1 month.

recipes.name: Goan Chicken Xacuti

steps.text: Marinate chicken with turmeric, salt and ginger-garlic paste.
Dry-roast red chillies and whole spices until fragrant; roast coconut separately until deep brown. Grind together with tamarind and water into a smooth paste.
Heat coconut oil in a pot and fry onion until golden; add tomato and cook down.
Add chicken and sear for 4 minutes, then add the xacuti paste and 300 ml water.
Cover and simmer until the chicken is tender and the gravy thick.

tips: Roasting the coconut properly is the secret to xacuti — go slow.
recipes.makeAhead: Keeps 3 days refrigerated; freezes for a month.

recipes.name: Bengali Kosha Chicken

steps.text: Marinate chicken with curd, turmeric, chilli powder, ginger-garlic paste and salt.
Heat mustard oil to smoking, then lower heat; add whole spices and jaggery and let it caramelise lightly.
Add sliced onion and fry until golden-brown; add grated onion and tomato and cook down.
Add the chicken with its marinade; "kosha" (slow-roast) on medium-low, stirring often, until the masala turns dark and oil surfaces.
Add cumin, coriander, green chilli and a splash of water; cover and cook until tender. Finish with garam masala.

tips: Heating mustard oil to smoking removes its raw pungency.
recipes.makeAhead: Refrigerate up to 3 days; flavours deepen overnight.

recipes.name: Bengali Light Chicken Curry with Bottle Gourd

steps.text: Rub chicken with turmeric and salt.
Heat mustard oil in the cooker until smoking; lower heat, add bay leaf and cardamom, then onion and cook until light brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste, tomato and the powdered spices with a splash of water; cook until oil separates.
Add chicken and sear for 4 minutes, then the bottle gourd, green chilli and 400 ml water. Pressure cook for 2 whistles; release naturally.
Adjust salt, garnish with coriander. The jhol should be thin and soupy.

tips: Light and gut-friendly; bottle gourd adds volume with very few calories.
recipes.makeAhead: Keeps 2 days refrigerated.

recipes.name: Air-Fryer Tandoori Chicken

ingredients.note: leg and thigh pieces, skinless, deep slashes

steps.text: First marinade: rub chicken with lemon juice, salt and chilli powder, pushing into the slashes.
Second marinade: mix hung curd, ginger-garlic paste, garam masala, cumin, kasuri methi, turmeric and 15 g mustard oil; coat the chicken and refrigerate (overnight is best).
Air-fry at 200°C for 22 minutes, flipping at 11 minutes and basting with the remaining mustard oil.
For char, air-fry 3 more minutes at 200°C, then rest 3 minutes before serving with onion rings and lemon.

tips: Thick hung curd keeps the marinade from dripping off and burning.
recipes.makeAhead: Marinate up to 24 hours; cooked chicken keeps 3 days and is great shredded into salads.

recipes.name: Air-Fryer Chicken Tikka with Peppers

steps.text: Whisk hung curd with roasted besan, ginger-garlic paste, spices, kasuri methi, lemon, salt and 10 g mustard oil. Add chicken, capsicum and onion; marinate.
Thread alternately on short skewers that fit your basket (or lay directly in the basket).
Air-fry at 200°C for 12 minutes, turning and brushing with the remaining oil at 6 minutes.
Air-fry 2–3 more minutes for charred edges; sprinkle chaat-style with lemon and cumin.

tips: Roasting the besan removes its raw taste and helps the marinade cling.
recipes.makeAhead: Marinate overnight for meal-prep; cook fresh.

recipes.name: Punjabi Spinach Chicken

steps.text: Blanch spinach with green chilli for 2 minutes, plunge in cold water, then blend to a coarse puree.
Heat oil in a kadai, crackle cumin, add onion and cook until golden; add ginger-garlic and sauté.
Add tomato puree, turmeric, chilli powder and salt; cook until oil separates. Add chicken and cook on medium for 8 minutes.
Stir in the spinach puree and a splash of water; simmer covered until the chicken is tender.
Finish with garam masala, crushed kasuri methi and the ghee.

tips: Blanch briefly and cool fast to keep the saag bright green.
Keto-friendly and high in iron and folate.
recipes.makeAhead: Keeps 3 days refrigerated; freezes well.

recipes.name: Chicken Besan Cheela

steps.text: Whisk besan, egg whites, spices, salt and about 120 ml water into a smooth pourable batter; rest.
Fold in the shredded chicken, onion, tomato, spinach, green chilli and coriander.
Heat a tawa, smear a little oil, pour a ladle of batter and spread to a thick pancake. Cook covered on medium until the base is golden.
Drizzle oil around the edges, flip and cook the other side. Repeat to make 4 cheelas.

tips: Use leftover tandoori chicken for extra flavour.
recipes.makeAhead: Boil and shred the chicken the night before.

recipes.name: Air-Fryer Chicken Seekh Kebab

steps.text: Combine all ingredients except ghee and knead for 3–4 minutes until sticky. Chill to firm up.
With wet hands, shape into 9 long kebabs around skewers (or as flat logs without skewers).
Brush with ghee and air-fry at 200°C for 12 minutes, turning and brushing again at 6 minutes.
Rest 2 minutes; serve with mint chutney and onion rings.

tips: Squeezing water from the onion stops the kebabs from falling apart.
recipes.makeAhead: Shape and freeze raw kebabs on a tray; air-fry from frozen at 190°C for 16 minutes.

recipes.name: Air-Fryer Murgh Malai Tikka

steps.text: Rub chicken with ginger-garlic paste, lemon and salt; rest.
Blend hung curd, cheese, cashew paste, green chilli, pepper, cardamom and nutmeg until creamy. Coat the chicken and marinate.
Air-fry at 200°C for 12 minutes, flipping and basting with butter at 6 minutes.
Air-fry 2 more minutes for light golden spots; do not over-char — malai tikka should stay pale.

tips: Use breast and pull it out the moment it is done to keep it juicy.
recipes.makeAhead: Marinate overnight in the fridge.

recipes.name: Air-Fryer Chilli Chicken (Dry)

steps.text: Mix chicken with egg white, 10 g soy sauce, pepper, salt and cornflour. Rest.
Spray or brush with 5 g garlic oil and air-fry at 200°C for 12 minutes, shaking/flipping at 6 minutes.
Heat remaining garlic oil in a kadai on high; stir-fry ginger and green chilli for 30 seconds, then capsicum for 2 minutes so it stays crunchy.
Add remaining soy sauce, vinegar and chilli sauce, then the air-fried chicken; toss on high for 1 minute.
Toss in spring onion greens and serve immediately.

tips: Low-FODMAP as written (garlic oil + spring onion greens). Keep the heat high for that wok flavour.

recipes.name: Indo-Chinese Chicken Cabbage Salad

steps.text: Poach chicken in salted simmering water with a slice of ginger until cooked through; rest and shred.
Whisk soy sauce, vinegar, chilli sauce, lemon juice, sesame oil and grated ginger into a dressing.
Toss cabbage, carrot, capsicum, bean sprouts and spring onion greens with the shredded chicken.
Pour over the dressing, toss well and top with toasted sesame seeds.

tips: Low-FODMAP; keep cabbage portion to around 75 g per serving for sensitive guts.
recipes.makeAhead: Poach chicken and cut vegetables up to 2 days ahead; dress just before eating.

recipes.name: Chicken Poha

steps.text: Rinse poha in a sieve, drain and leave to soften with a pinch of salt and turmeric.
Heat oil; roast peanuts, then crackle mustard seeds and curry leaves. Add onion and green chilli and sauté until soft.
Add capsicum, tomato and the shredded chicken; cook for 3 minutes.
Add the poha and remaining salt, toss gently, cover and steam on low.
Finish with lemon juice and coriander.

tips: Use leftover tandoori or stew chicken for a 10-minute breakfast.

recipes.name: Chicken Keema Omelette

steps.text: Heat half the oil, sauté onion and green chilli, add the mince with turmeric, garam masala and a pinch of salt; cook until dry and crumbly.
Stir in tomato and spinach for a minute until wilted; remove the filling.
Beat eggs and whites with pepper and salt. Heat the remaining oil, pour in half the egg and cook on medium until almost set.
Spoon half the keema over one side, fold and cook 1 more minute. Repeat for the second omelette.

tips: Keto-friendly: about 3 g net carbs per serving.
recipes.makeAhead: Cook the keema filling in bulk; it keeps 3 days refrigerated.

recipes.name: Air-Fryer Chicken Kachumber Salad

steps.text: Coat chicken with lactose-free curd, garlic oil, chilli powder, half the cumin, pepper and half the salt. Marinate.
Air-fry at 190°C for 14 minutes, flipping at 7 minutes; rest 5 minutes and slice.
Toss cucumber, tomato, lettuce, spring onion greens, mint and coriander with lemon juice, olive oil, remaining cumin and salt.
Top with sliced chicken and pumpkin seeds.

tips: Low-FODMAP and keto. Pack the dressing separately for office lunches.
recipes.makeAhead: Air-fry chicken for 3 days at once; assemble salads fresh.

recipes.name: Air-Fryer Chicken Egg Muffins

steps.text: Whisk eggs and whites with turmeric, pepper, chilli powder and salt.
Grease 12 silicone muffin cups and divide the chicken and vegetables among them; pour over the egg and top with cheese.
Air-fry at 160°C for 12–14 minutes until puffed and set in the centre (no flipping needed).
Cool 2 minutes before unmoulding. 3 muffins per serving.

tips: Low-FODMAP and keto. Lower temperature keeps them from browning before the centre sets.
recipes.makeAhead: Refrigerate up to 4 days; reheat at 160°C for 3 minutes.
